entries.reason: the request whose answer is the feature print observation whose element type VNElementTypeSize answers for. It is a VNImageBasedRequest, as its own header declares, and it had exactly one revision in 13.0, so the port's own revision table already places it. The descriptor behind it is Apple's own learned model and there is no source for it
entries.effect: the class is there: NSClassFromString answers it, alloc makes one, and it is a kind of VNRequest that a handler takes. Running it answers VNErrorNotImplemented from the request path
entries.source: the Vision census of the two releases this port deploys on, which finds no image naming Vision at all in 6.1.3 or 4.3, with 11.0 and 12.0 read in the same run as the control, and the SDK's own annotation of ios(13.0) with its single revision; facts/Vision/Absence.md sections 1 and 4

entries.reason: the request whose answer carries the two animal identifiers above. It is a VNImageBasedRequest, which is what its own header declares, and it had exactly one revision in 13.0, so the port's own revision table already places it. entries.reason: how many bytes one element of a feature print's data takes: 4 for a float, 8 for a double, and 0 for the unknown case and for every argument the enumeration does not name. The widths are sizeof of the two types rather than written numbers, so the answer is the width on the release that asks
entries.effect: the function is there and answers 4, 8 and 0 for the arguments measured, and a caller reading elementCount can multiply by it
entries.source: this host's own Vision, asked for the arguments 0 to 4 and answering 0, 4, 8, 0, 0, by tools/vision/probe130.m compiled for Mac Catalyst; facts/Vision/Absence.md section 4, with the command beside its output

entries.reason: which constellations of face landmarks a revision of the request maps a face with: revisions 1 to 3 for the 65-point constellation, revision 3 alone also for the 76-point one, and not-defined for none of them. The port answers Apple's whole table rather than narrowing it to the revisions it carries, because a revision the port cannot run is refused by the request handler with VNErrorUnsupportedRevision, and that is a different question from the one this method asks
entries.effect: the method is there and answers Apple's answers for every pair measured, including NO for the not-defined constellation and for any revision outside 1 to 3
entries.source: this host's own Vision, asked for every pair of a revision from 1 to 4 and a constellation from not-defined through 76 points, by tools/vision/probe130.m compiled for Mac Catalyst; facts/Vision/Absence.md section 4, with the command beside its output

entries.reason: whether the operation point chosen by a recall has a minimum precision. This port runs a Core ML classifier, which answers one score per class, and a precision and recall curve is those same scores swept across thresholds of themselves: there is no set of scores here and so no operation point to ask about
entries.effect: the method is there and answers NO, which is the answer to a question about a curve this port's classifications do not have
entries.source: the SDK header's own rule for the addition these three members belong to, which makes hasPrecisionRecallCurve the gate and says the other two must not be sent when it is NO, and this port's request path in VNHandlers.m, which builds one VNClassificationObservation per class from one score and keeps no scores of its own; facts/Vision/Absence.md section 5

entries.reason: the same asked the other way round, and the same answer for the same reason: with one score per class there is no operation point
entries.effect: the method is there and answers NO

entries.reason: the progress a long request reports through. The build emits the protocol's metadata into the library, so the name resolves at run time; the port does not adopt the protocol on its own VNRecognizeTextRequest, because it cannot run a text recognition and so has no progress to report, and a progressHandler that is stored and never called would answer a caller exactly as no protocol at all would
entries.effect: the protocol is there: NSProtocolFromString answers it by name. The port's own VNRecognizeTextRequest does not conform to it, and its row says so
entries.source: this host's own Vision, where NSProtocolFromString answers for the protocol and answers nil for a name it does not carry, by tools/vision/probe130.m compiled for Mac Catalyst; facts/Vision/Absence.md section 4, with the command beside its output
